note:
FEATURE / GAMEPLAY ISSUE: Add the first playable quest to Kentridge by recreating the kid-in-the-well quest from the original jlashmet/mounting-force game using the quest infrastructure that already exists on master. Do not create a second quest framework. Inspect the legacy quest/content first and preserve its recognizable scenario, trigger, NPC/well interaction, progression, and dialogue where practical while adapting it to the current Kentridge, WorldBuilder, Story, interaction, and Game.Quests APIs.

Completing the quest must award one item exactly once. There is no reusable inventory subsystem currently found on master, so add the smallest reusable item/inventory runtime needed to own and query player items; keep this separate from Kentridge-specific quest code and from UI presentation.

Add a minimal inventory viewer using the existing input/menu/UI conventions. The player must be able to open and close it and see owned items as small square icon tiles. The reward item must appear in that inventory after quest completion. No equipment, item usage, drag/drop, crafting, vendors, sorting/filtering, quest journal, or broad item-system work is required for this slice.

ARCHITECTURE BOUNDARY: Reuse Assets/Game/Quests/Api and Assets/Game/Quests/Runtime plus the existing Story/Campaign quest seams. If authored QuestDefinitions are not yet composed into the live CampaignRuntime/QuestRuntime path, finish that reusable wiring rather than tracking this quest with Kentridge-local booleans. Route normal production interaction observations/events into quest progression and quest completion into the inventory reward path. World/NPC/well composition must follow the standard Kentridge/WorldBuilder path rather than scene-only bespoke logic.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) Kentridge contains a playable kid-in-the-well quest recognizably based on the original mounting-force version; (2) the existing quest system on master owns quest state/progression; (3) normal gameplay interaction can start and complete the quest; (4) completion grants exactly one reward item and repeated interactions cannot duplicate it; (5) the player can open/close inventory and see owned items as square icons; (6) the reward appears in the inventory; (7) focused behavioral regressions cover quest progression, exactly-once reward, and inventory add/read behavior; and (8) the built-application Kentridge harness loads the scene and verifies the quest/reward/inventory flow without startup/runtime exceptions.
